rv.q: The show remains what it always has been — a crowd-pleaser with no serious theatrical ambitions.
Its saving grace is a certain good-natured goofiness that somehow tampers the deep-rooted sexism of the L.A. metal scene.
It all looks stupendous under Jason Lyons's arena-rock lighting, resulting in a fist-pumping spectacle that can be enjoyed by old and new fans alike.
Rock of Ages hasn't lost any of its cheeseball charm.
Costumes by Gregory Gale reveal a lot of skin, but the production as a whole, as directed by Kristin Hanggi, seems afraid to show any heart.
If you wanna rock, now's the time to do it.
